findings.quote: whether they knew that he was fighting unfairly
findings.problem: Greek: πότερον οὐ συνοίδασιν αὐτῷ ποιοῦντι τὰ δίκαια κατὰ τὴν ἄθλησιν - 'do they not realize that he (Cleitomachus, in indirect speech) is acting justly/fairly in the contest'. The English drops the οὐ and inverts the sense to 'unfairly'.
findings.proposed_fix: whether they were not aware that he himself was fighting fairly

units.note: Also: ἁπάντων ἀγὼν μικρὸς γίνεται (the 'whole crowd thrown into excitement') is an obscure idiom; English is an acceptable gloss, left alone.

findings.quote: in defiance of every principle of justice.
findings.problem: Greek ends πρότερος *** - the text breaks off after 'first' (lacuna); the English closes the sentence as if complete.
findings.proposed_fix: in defiance of every principle of justice [the text breaks off here].
